content.text: No Vendor convenience or suspension-for-convenience right exists anywhere. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional, no-cause election to terminate the Agreement at any time — a convenience right even though the word "convenience" is not used — with service simply continuing until the last day of the month following the month of notice (roughly 30-60 days' run-off). That is at or better than the fallback notice window of 60-90 days, and no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge appears anywhere in the Agreement, so the three-months-of-fees fee cap is comfortably satisfied. On the Vendor side, TrueLink has no mid-term termination-for-convenience right: Section 13 (p0078) permits mid-term cutting-off of Sections 2 and 3 only for Client breach/default events (for cause), and the only other exit is the mutual auto-renewal non-renewal notice given "no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year," whose effect is expressly tied to the end of the then-current one-year term — that is natural-term non-renewal reviewed under RENEWAL, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so we do not flag it twice here. The initial term is one year, so the walk-away concern about no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term does not arise. Falling short of the preferred position only in that there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; this is immaterial because Section 5(a) (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with invoices "paid within 15 days of receipt," so fees are not prepaid. The clause therefore sits at (and in the Customer's favour, above) the fallback and we would not redline it.
